name: Calendly
tagline: Scheduling links for booking meetings without back-and-forth email

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Standard listed at $12/seat/month monthly and $10/seat/month annually.

verdictSummary: A single-user booking page is easy; production-grade scheduling needs OAuth, availability rules, time zones, reminders, payments, team routing, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Connect calendar, publish event-type pages, let guests choose available slots, create calendar events, and send reminders.
whatYouLose: polished Google/Outlook OAuth kept working for you
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because double-booking or missed meeting invites is costly.

priorArt.name: cal.com
priorArt.desc: open-source Calendly; self-host and skip the OAuth pain

alternatives.name: Cal.com Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited solo event types, calendars and bookings, with payments and notifications; team routing costs money.

alternatives.name: Google Calendar appointment schedules
alternatives.desc: One bare appointment page inside the calendar you already use; reminders, payments and polish are paid.

alternatives.name: Koalendar Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited booking pages and two calendar connections; payments, forms, reminders and team routing are paid.

alternatives.name: TidyCal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited one-person booking types and paid bookings on one calendar; group meetings and fancy emails cost extra.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

alternatives.name: Zoho Bookings Free
alternatives.desc: A real one-person booking desk with forms, reminders and two-way sync; staff and payment plumbing cost extra.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cal.diy
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Self-hostable, yes; also explicitly a hobbyist, non-production fork that expects database and security expertise.

notes: The booking page is easy. Calendar-sync OAuth is where weekends go to die; be honest with yourself about that before starting.
prompt:
Build me a personal booking page like Calendly. Requirements:

- A public /book page showing my available slots for the next 14 days; visitors
  pick one, enter name + email + note, and get a confirmation page.
- Availability = weekly rules in a config file (e.g. Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00,
  30-min slots, 15-min buffer between meetings, my timezone) minus existing
  bookings, rendered in the visitor's local timezone.
- Google Calendar sync via OAuth (credentials in .env): busy events block slots,
  and confirmed bookings are created in my calendar with the visitor invited and
  a Google Meet link attached. Warn me in the README: this OAuth app setup is
  the fiddly part · budget an hour for the Google Cloud console alone.
- Email confirmations to both sides via SMTP creds in .env.
- Cancel/reschedule links with a signed token in the email.
- SQLite storage, one Node process, no accounts, no framework lock-in.
